title: Code interviews for weekly take-home programming assignments
summary: Students attend short in-person oral assessments about five required take-home Python assignments. TAs ask students to trace, compare, debug, extend, or rewrite aspects of their own work, providing evidence of understanding when take-home code may have been AI-assisted.

sources.title: Code Interviews: Design and Evaluation of a More Authentic Assessment for Introductory Programming Assignments
sources.evidence_quote: Code interviews are a type of live oral assessment for programming.

assessment.summary: Explain and extend recently submitted take-home programming work in a brief live interview with a teaching assistant.
student_actions: Trace a test case through their program.
Compare their approach with another solution.
Find a bug in a supplied solution.
Write code for an isomorphic problem.

outputs.artifact: Live tracing, debugging, or coding response

timing.release: On the due date of each of five weekly programming assignments

student_role.description: The live interview is an integrity-oriented supplement to take-home work in the GenAI era; the paper does not report an explicit AI-use rule for the interview itself.

assessment_system_role: The oral assessment provides independent evidence that the student can explain and extend submitted code.

grading.method: Teaching assistants apply a four-level proficiency rubric.

reported_results: Winter interviews were conducted in groups of three or four; spring variants used pairs or individual interviews.
Spring results were 30% Exemplary, 63% Satisfactory, and 7% Approaching.

provenance.extraction_method: Full PDF read from pdftotext output.

evidence_excerpts.quote: Code interviews are a type of live oral assessment for programming.
